channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Amazing Abstracts 2026 · MVA Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, for artists who have declared their independence from portraying reality — abstract work built on line, shape, colour, form and gestural mark, from drip paintings and colour fields to geometric designs and abstract patterns found in nature, architecture and human activity. Photography and photo-based work are accepted alongside painting, printmaking, mixed media, drawing and sculpture. Open to US residents 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works. Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award with a special exhibit in the gallery's second exhibition room, an honorable mention carrying free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity drawn from all artists shown during the year. The gallery takes 30% commission on sales and artists cover shipping both ways. Exhibition runs December 19, 2026 – January 16, 2027. — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Variations of Yellow 2026 · MVA Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, built around a single colour. Yellow carries warmth, joy, spontaneity and optimism — and, in its other register, cowardice and deceit; the gallery asks how the colour works in your practice, whether it floods the frame or appears in a single object, whether it is decorative or structural. Realistic or imaginary, representational or abstract, all interpretations are welcome. Photography and photo collage are accepted alongside painting, printmaking, mixed media, drawing and sculpture. Open to US residents 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works. Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award with a special exhibit in the gallery's second exhibition room, an honorable mention carrying free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity. Exhibition runs December 19, 2026 – January 16, 2027. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Changing Seasons · MVA Gallery
item.description: National juried exhibition at MVA Gallery (Modern Visual Arts) in historic Bethlehem, Pennsylvania, on seasonal change as a transformative force. The gallery invites three layers of response: nature (landscapes and seascapes through the year, the rhythms of growth, transition and decay), human activity (swimming, skiing, picnicking, gardening — or figures struggling against weather and terrain), and emotional effect (spring as renewal, summer as freedom, autumn as melancholy, winter as isolation). Photography and photo-based work are accepted alongside painting, printmaking, mixed media, drawing and sculpture. Open to US residents 18 and over; submit 3 to 9 works. Awards include a $200 Director's Choice, an Art of Distinction award with a special exhibit in the gallery's second exhibition room, an honorable mention carrying free entry to a future MVA show, and an annual grand prize of a New York City exhibition opportunity. Exhibition runs December 19, 2026 – January 16, 2027. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: $35 (3 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + NYC exhibition.

item.title: Unbound 2: Anything Goes · Studio ACE
item.description: Second edition of ACE Gallery's open-themed juried exhibition in Oceanside, California, returning after an enthusiastic response to the inaugural show. The gallery asks artists to release expectations, defy their own rules and submit the work that excites them most — Unbound honours process over perfection and passion over polish, welcoming confident statements, quiet reflections and unexpected juxtapositions alike. Photography sits alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, printmaking, mixed media and fully experimental work. Studio ACE is an arts-education nonprofit founded in 2016 that runs free art programmes for neurodivergent children, teens and adults; ACE Gallery, its exhibition space, opened in early 2024 and shows both emerging and established artists. Submit 3 to 20 works. Accepted work is notified August 21, with drop-off September 11–12. Exhibition runs September 19 – October 22, 2026, with an opening reception on September 19. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $25 (3 works) + $10 each additional. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Art Comes Alive 2026 · ADC Fine Art
item.description: Seventeenth edition of ADC Fine Art's annual exhibition and awards gala, held in the gallery's 13,000 sq ft space in Cincinnati's Over-the-Rhine and long nicknamed the 'Academy Awards for Artists'. Around 250 living artists are shown across all mediums, photography included. What distinguishes it from a typical juried show is the award structure: ADC puts the total at over $450,000, though most of that is its own services valued in-house rather than cash — ten gallery representation contracts valued at $8,500 each, two solo shows, six group shows, print and digital magazine features and SmartSell memberships, alongside $74,100 in juror awards and $175,000 in purchase awards. The jury is drawn from ADC's own staff — president Litsa Spanos, gallery director Annie Kautz, marketing director Amy Scalia and assistant gallery director Chance Smith — with more jurors to be announced. Entry is $25 per work, with the last entry free on applications of four or more. Results are announced October 2, work arrives at the gallery by October 16, and the opening night and awards ceremony fall on November 7. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: $25 per work. Prize: $175,000 purchase awards + Solo exhibition.

item.title: Changing Asia 2026 · China Daily Asia Pacific
item.description: The Changing Asia photo exhibition, organised by China Daily with the Asia News Network, returns with the theme "Moments of Connection: Smiles and Hands of the Asia-Pacific" — a phrase drawn from the 2026 APEC leaders' meeting slogan, and a brief that asks for real interactions: collaboration, trade, mutual assistance, cultural exchange. Within that frame the call keeps its long-standing threads — the social, economic, environmental and cultural shifts reshaping the continent, stories of resilience told through individual communities, and Asia's diversity documented in its contrasts as much as its connections. Entry is free and open to photographers worldwide; work must have been made since 1 January 2023, and basic colour correction and filters are accepted. Selected images are shown in the exhibition, published in the accompanying photo book and awarded a certificate. Earlier editions launched in Bangkok (2022) and Jakarta (2023) before moving online in 2024, which drew over 1,400 submissions from more than 40 countries. The 2026 exhibition opens on 26 October at the Shenzhen Research Institute of The Chinese University of Hong Kong, ahead of the APEC meeting. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition + Photo book.

item.title: Fire · A Photographer's Place
item.description: Fire as an elemental force but also as an idea. The gallery invites photographic work that engages with fire as metaphor, condition and experience rather than simply as subject matter — images that consider the elemental through the psychological, the social, the environmental or the poetic. Work that reveals fire through gesture, light, atmosphere, colour, landscape, portraiture, abstraction or narrative is welcome, where the photograph evokes rather than describes. Not every fire burns. Open to photographers of all levels, in colour or black and white. Selected work hangs in Gallery X at the front of the space in Raleigh from September 4 to 30, 2026, with an opening reception on September 4, and is then presented on the gallery website year-round. Accepted artists may optionally have their work printed in-house on the gallery's Canon imagePROGRAF Pro-1100. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: $35 (up to 5 images). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Monochrome · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Curated international group exhibition of monochromatic photography — not limited to black and white but including sepia, cyan and other single-colour tonal ranges, where the absence of a colour range carries meaning as a deliberate artistic choice rather than a technical necessity. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD; founder/director of PH21 Gallery, Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian). One Curator's Choice winner receives three complimentary entries to future PH21 themed calls, and up to three honourable mentions are announced. Reduced rates of €15 (early bird) or €20 apply for students, unwaged applicants and those from low-income economies. Early bird deadline September 7, final deadline September 14. Exhibition at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter, November 14 – December 8, 2026. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: €25–€50. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Guildford Festival of the Arts 2026
item.description: Open call for the 2026 edition of this Surrey arts festival, accepting any visual art of any medium that can be displayed in a gallery or on a screen — photography included. There is no set theme. Two tracks run in parallel: an Open Call for artists aged 18 and over, and a separate Student Open Call. The 2026 judging panel is Sally Varah MBE DL, Councillor Jane Tyson (Mayor of Guildford), artist Monica Popham and photographer Andy Newbold. Everyone's first submission is free; further artworks go through a separate paid form. Alongside the £1,000 first prize there is a £500 runner-up prize, a £150 gift voucher for the student winner and an exhibition at New House Art Space for the Public Vote winner. Selected artists are notified by email in late August or early September and may sell work through the festival team during the festival, on which a 15% commission is retained to fund the following year's edition. Artists should submit once; a series, diptych or triptych should be sent as a single image encompassing the whole piece. The inaugural 2025 festival drew over 2,400 visits across 20 venues. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Pretty Ugly — Student Photography Competition 2026/27 · ILFORD Photo
item.description: A darkroom print competition asking students to explore the idea that ugliness is often just a matter of perspective. A rough texture, an unusual face, a forgotten space — under the right conditions the overlooked becomes extraordinary, and perceived imperfections such as scars, wear and age can tell powerful stories of resilience and character. Entrants are challenged to question first impressions and capture their own interpretation of 'pretty ugly'. All images must be shot on ILFORD or Kentmere black and white film and hand-printed by the student in the darkroom on ILFORD or Kentmere black and white papers; digital submissions are not accepted and prints must be posted with an entry label firmly attached to the back of each. Minimum print size is 8x10 inches, and images that have won other competitions or been published by a third party are not eligible. Multiple entries are encouraged, and lecturers may bundle a class's prints in one package. Open to students of any age anywhere in the world taking a full or part-time course at a school, college or university; prints go to HARMAN technology in Mobberley, Cheshire, or to its Seattle address. ILFORD points students without darkroom access to its Pop-Up Darkrooms and community darkroom locator. — Deadline: January 31, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: £200 in ILFORD products + 35mm film camera.

item.title: Let Our Hearts Speak · Rethinking Eastern Europe
item.description: Open call for a collective publication from Rethinking Eastern Europe, an artist collective founded in 2024 by Polish visual artist Zula Rabikowska that now gathers around 50 artists from Central and Eastern Europe, the Balkans and the diaspora. Taking its title from bell hooks — 'when we love we can let our hearts speak' — the call invites work that engages with 'Eastern Europe' as a lived, shifting and often contested space: not only geography, but memory, inheritance, migration and emotional landscape. The publication brings together visual and written works reflecting on intimacy, love, identity, displacement and belonging, and understands the region as plural and expansive, shaped by diasporas, post-socialist realities and personal archives. Open to artists of any age, nationality, location and career stage, including those working outside institutions. Published in collective print and digital formats with careful artist attribution; fee waivers are available on request. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: £8 (waivers available). Prize: £150 + Publication.

item.title: James Balog Earth Vision Awards · Denver Art Museum
item.description: Juried prizes supporting photographers responding to today's complex environmental issues, organised and produced by the Denver Art Museum with funds endowed by James Balog and other donors, and awarded every two years. The awards recognise sustained commitment and significant accomplishment in photography that bears witness to the relationship between humans and the environment and challenges people to build healthier, more sustainable relationships with nature. A three-member jury of expert photo professionals reviews all entries and may contact entrants for clarification before final decisions; fabricated photographs, cloning, excessive colour manipulation and AI-generated content are not considered. First prize is $40,000 ($30,000 on award, $10,000 twelve to eighteen months later) and the finalist receives $25,000 ($19,000 on award, $6,000 later). Applicants submit a portfolio of 10 to 20 photographs — falling outside that range is grounds for disqualification — with an artist statement describing firsthand experience and the environmental significance of the work, an explanation of the intended project and its anticipated impact, and a resume or exhibition history. Open to photographers worldwide aged 21 or over; previous winners and finalists are not eligible. The call opens September 1, 2026, winners are announced in January 2027, and awards are presented at the Denver Art Museum in March 2027. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $40,000.

item.title: Women United ART PRIZE 2026 — Photography & Printmaking · Women United Art Movement
item.description: Annual international prize for women-identifying artists, with a dedicated Photography & Printmaking category covering all types of photography and printmaking including cyanotype. First place in each category receives USD 500 cash, an in-depth interview in Women United Art Magazine Special Edition 2026, a podcast interview, a virtual solo exhibition with 3D gallery tour, an artist directory profile, a USD 250 printing gift card, and free entries to 2027 opportunities. Second and third place receive interviews, an online group exhibit and virtual 3D tour. Places 4–10 are featured in the magazine and group exhibit. Regular entries close 31 August; a last-minute phase runs 1–15 September at higher fees. Fee waivers available for artists in countries affected by war, natural disaster, or the suppression of women’s rights. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: €16–€45. Prize: $500 + Publication + Exhibition.

item.title: Around, Above, Below · Van Der Plas Gallery
item.description: Group exhibition at Van Der Plas Gallery on Manhattan’s Lower East Side exploring perception and the experience of daily life as we move through urban environments, rural landscapes and the spaces in between. The show sets up a dialogue between the built environment and the natural world, asking artists to explore the balance between tension and harmony. Artists working in all media are encouraged to submit, including photography. On view 1–15 October 2026 with an opening reception on 1 October, 6–8pm. Submissions form part of the gallery’s year-round Open Call Program and remain in consideration for future exhibitions beyond this cycle. — Deadline: September 17, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: Maledetto Cane — Next Photobook Open Call
item.description: Rome-based independent photobook publisher autoproduzioni Maledetto Cane is looking for a photographic body of work with a coherent authorial visual language and the potential to be published as a monographic photobook. The selected body of work will be developed into a monograph by the press. All submissions are also considered for inclusion in Maledetto Cane #3, the third issue of the collective periodical. Submit a portfolio of no fewer than 40 JPEGs by email or WeTransfer, with a short synopsis or artist statement; a draft PDF of the proposed book may be included but is not required. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Photobook publication.

item.title: The Book Project: Landscape 2026 · Black Box Gallery
item.description: Juried call for a published hardbound photography book on landscape photography, part of Black Box Gallery’s Book Project series of focused hardbound books each built around a single theme. From grand landscapes to intimate details, the gallery is looking for work that demonstrates the photographer’s own connection to nature. Ten photographers will be selected with five photographs each. The 12 × 12 inch hardbound book is printed by Blurb and sold through the Black Box Gallery website. All rights to the photographs remain with the photographer and files are used only for the book printing. Photographers are notified 7–10 days after the deadline. Apply by paying the entry fee via PayPal and emailing your entry. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Publication in printed photobook.

item.title: Emerging Berlin · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: Year-round local open call from Fotografiska’s Emerging programme, dedicated to supporting and showcasing image-makers with a distinctive visual language whose photographic practice embodies, represents and shapes a part of Berlin. Selected artists are given a platform at Fotografiska Berlin through solo or group exhibitions. An emerging artist here means a photographer or image-maker whose work has not yet been presented in an institutional museum exhibition but who has already developed a recognisable visual language — the definition is not tied to age, years of experience or formal education, and includes self-taught artists and those working outside traditional pathways. The call has run on an ongoing basis since 12 March 2026; submissions are reviewed by the jury every six months, followed by a curation period of up to two weeks. Open to anyone 18 or over — the Berlin connection is a criterion for the work, not a residency requirement. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Emerging Stockholm · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: Year-round local open call from Fotografiska’s Emerging programme, running since 2023 and dedicated to supporting and showcasing early-career image-makers from across Sweden. Roughly three artists a year are invited to present their work within Fotografiska Stockholm’s exhibition programme, alongside opportunities for professional dialogue and development. Material is reviewed on an ongoing basis throughout the year, and only artists whose work moves forward in the internal review are contacted. Applicants must be 18 or over and based in Sweden. An emerging artist here means a photographer or image-maker whose work has not yet been presented in an institutional museum exhibition but who has already developed a recognisable visual language — not tied to age, years of experience or formal education, and including self-taught artists. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free. Prize: Fotografiska Stockholm exhibition.

item.title: Quinn Emanuel Silicon Valley Artist-in-Residence 2026
item.description: Four-month studio residency at Quinn Emanuel's Silicon Valley office in Redwood Shores for emerging and mid-career artists working in any medium, including photography. Two artists are selected per cycle and each receives $5,000 per month for four months ($20,000 total) plus a materials allowance of up to $1,500. The residency begins November 2026; a one-month exhibition follows, mounted with curator Alexis Hyde in a venue agreed with the artists, and work may be offered for sale. The studio is an office inside the Silicon Valley location, in a 24/7 keycard-access building with parking if needed. Open only to artists living in the greater Bay Area, as regular in-person studio use is expected; international artists may apply but must secure their own visas. Preference goes to underrepresented artists in the early or middle stages of their career. No education requirement, and the firm will make accommodations for disabled artists. Apply by email with a 500-word proposal, a CV and an 8–10 image portfolio as a single PDF under 20MB. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $20,000 stipend + $1,500 materials + Exhibition.

item.title: Opulent Mobility 2026
item.description: Opulent Mobility is an international annual exhibit that asks artists to re-imagine disability as opulent and powerful rather than merely functional. The 2026 focus is disabled joy — as the call puts it, at a time when rights are being dismantled and images erased, deliberate acts of joy are powerful and essential. Curated by founder A. Laura Brody with disability arts activist and photographer Anthony Tusler, and supported by the Numotion Foundation. Two-dimensional and sculptural work, music files and performances on digital media are all accepted; photographers may submit digital files rather than shipping prints, which makes the show genuinely open to international entrants. A flat $20 fee covers gallery rental and insurance for up to ten works, and is waived on request if it causes hardship. The exhibit runs December 6–20, 2026 in person in Los Angeles and online; the gallery takes 30% of any sale. Accessibility is built in: artwork descriptions in text and audio, and ASL interpreters at the opening and the online artist talk. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $20 (up to 10 works), waived on request. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Solo Exhibition September 2026 · All About Photo
item.description: Monthly featured photographer showcase. Winner receives a full month online solo exhibition (September 1–30, 2026), permanent gallery presence, exclusive interview, social media promotion, newsletter feature, international press coverage, and commission-free sales. Submit a cohesive project or portfolio of 6–14 images. — Deadline: August 11, 2026. Fee: $45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Photography Now 2027 · CICA Museum
item.description: International photography exhibition at CICA Museum, the contemporary art museum in Gimpo, South Korea, open to artists worldwide. The call spans traditional and digital photography through experimental practice, framed around photography's role as representation, medium, expression and communication. Submission is free by email — up to five JPEGs and/or three video links plus a bio. Selected digital works are printed on A3 foam board and installed by the museum's curators; artists sending physical prints or installation pieces ship at their own cost and are asked to keep 2D work under 1 m on the longest side. Accepted artists contribute $78 USD (110,000 KRW) per work toward show processing and maintenance. The exhibition runs April 7–25, 2027 at the museum. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: Free to submit; $78 per accepted work. Prize: Museum exhibition.

item.title: Mythos Negra — Dark Myths · ShadowBoxX Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at ShadowBoxX Gallery in Waukegan, north of Chicago, for artists working in analog media. Mythos Negra explores the shadowed realms of myth, superstition and folklore that emerge from humanity's deepest fears — the femme fatale whose allure brings ruin, the tragic figure complicit in their own downfall, the wrathful deity dispensing arbitrary punishment. Personal myths and ritual are equally welcome. Eligible work includes film-based and darkroom photography alongside painting, printmaking, sculpture, collage, textile and other physically produced processes; digital artwork, digital manipulation and AI-generated work are not considered. Founded by artist Michael E. Voss, the gallery runs monthly group and solo shows and says it works to keep artists' shipping and display costs down. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: $20, $5 each additional image. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: America the Bountiful — Photography Show 2026 · Coastal Arts League
item.description: Annual juried photography show at the Coastal Arts League's public gallery on Main Street in Half Moon Bay, a volunteer-run nonprofit that has served the Coastside for over forty years. This year's theme is America the Bountiful; prints on any surface are welcome, up to three entries per artist. Open to Bay Area artists 18 and over, with work hand-delivered September 28 and collected November 2. Three merit awards of $150, $100 and $50 are given. All exhibited work must be for sale and must not have been shown recently at the gallery; the League retains a 30% commission. The show runs October 1 – November 2, 2026 with a reception on October 3. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: $55 ($45 members), $5 each additional. Prize: $150 / $100 / $50.

item.title: Lines & Layers · Falkirk Cultural Center
item.description: Fall juried show in the light-filled second-floor galleries of Falkirk Cultural Center, an 1888 Queen Anne estate on eleven acres in San Rafael, listed on the National Historic Register and run by the City of San Rafael since 1974. Lines guide the eye and define form; layers add depth, texture and history — artists are invited to explore either or the relationship between the two, from patterns in nature to bold geometric composition and richly textured surfaces. Photography is welcome alongside drawing, painting, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, fiber and mixed media. Open to artists living in the nine Bay Area counties, with up to three works made in the past two years and not previously shown at Falkirk. The exhibition runs September 11 – October 23, 2026, opening during San Rafael's Art Walk. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: $40, $7.50 each additional. Prize: $100 / $75 / $50.

item.title: That's Absurd. · Alliance for the Arts
item.description: Absurdist open call from the Alliance for the Arts, the nonprofit visual and performing arts centre on McGregor Boulevard in Fort Myers, running since 1975. The show invites work that treads the line between meaning and meaninglessness — collapsing expectations, twisting logic, turning the familiar unrecognisable. Surreal imagery, exaggerated forms, inconclusive narratives and playful disruptions of reality are all fair game, in serious humour and methodical chaos. Open to all artists everywhere, one to three works, with photography among the accepted categories alongside painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, glass, printmaking, fiber and digital media. Absurdest in Show takes a $200 cash award, with four Most Absurd prizes across figurative, food-related, 2D and 3D work. On display November 6–28, 2026. — Deadline: October 4, 2026. Fee: $20, $5 each additional. Prize: $200 + Exhibition.

item.title: 31st Annual Gateway to the Rockies Art Show · Aurora Artists Guild
item.description: Long-running juried show and sale from the Aurora Artists Guild, a volunteer nonprofit of photographers and 2-D artists in Aurora, Colorado. Photography has its own dedicated category — traditional, digital or computer-enhanced — judged alongside separate 2-D and Miniatures categories, with up to three works per category and nine in total. Janet Schreiner jurors all three. Awards for photography are Best of Show, 1st, 2nd, 3rd and honourable mentions, with monetary awards and gifts set by entry numbers and sponsor contributions. Accepted work is hand-delivered to Aurora Central Library on October 31; only Miniatures may be mailed. The show runs November 6 – December 4, 2026, with the reception and awards ceremony on November 7. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images), $5 each additional. Prize: Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: PLAYFUL · Arc Gallery & Studios
item.description: Arc Gallery's 2027 national juried exhibition, built around the playful spirit — light-hearted, lively, spontaneous work full of fun, amusement and wit, taking its cue from Claes Oldenburg. The gallery is looking for creative play and grown-up mischief: bright colour, whimsical typography, funny imagery, sly innuendo, interactive works that invite audience participation, work that captures street art or spontaneous street photography, and work that expresses child-like wonder and game-play. Photography is among the accepted categories alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, assemblage, collage, mixed media, fibre art and artist books; jewellery, video, film, performance and works needing an external power source are not accepted. Juried by Jennifer Farris, owner of STUDIO Gallery in San Francisco. Three works judged the most imaginative interpretations of the theme each receive $250, a juror's award ribbon, a recognition certificate and the show catalogue; all selected work, gallery and online, appears in the exhibition catalogue. Entry is $35 for one to three images, maximum two entries per artist. Open to artists residing in the United States. Exhibition runs June 19 – July 17, 2027 at Arc Gallery, 1246 Folsom Street, San Francisco. — Deadline: March 29, 2027. Fee: $35 (1–3 works). Prize: $250 + Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Call for Solo or Group Exhibits 2027 · Huron Valley Arts
item.description: Huron Valley Arts, a 501(c)(3) arts council serving Michigan's Huron Valley communities for over 25 years, is taking proposals for its 2027 gallery year in Steeple Hall, the exhibition space inside the historic Highland Station House. The call is open to all artists, groups and curators working in any traditional or non-traditional visual arts medium — photography is explicitly among the accepted media — with no restriction on genre, subject matter or content. Artists may apply individually or as a cohesive group through a designated leader. Those selected exhibit for roughly one to two months, and HVA provides advertising plus a 'Meet the Artist' wine and appetizer reception planned in collaboration with the artist. Applicants submit 8–20 images; up to four entries per artist. Hanging works are limited to 25 lbs and 48 inches in any direction, work must be hand-delivered, and unsold pieces collected in person; the gallery suggests pricing in the $100–$500 range, which sells best at the venue. The jury fee is $30, with scholarships available to waive it on request. Applying early is encouraged — HVA reserves the option of contracting with artists before the published notification date. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: $30 (waivers available). Prize: Solo or group exhibition.

item.title: Small Works Members Show · Woman Made Gallery
item.description: Woman Made Gallery's end-of-year small-works exhibition, open to all current WMG members of any gender working in any medium — photography included. Each artist submits JPEGs of three works, one of which is guaranteed a place in the show. Work must measure 20 inches or under on its longest side, be priced at $400 or less and listed for sale, and must not have been previously shown at WMG; recent work is encouraged but not required, and a general artist's statement is needed. Selected by the WMG Program Committee. The exhibition runs November 21 – December 19, 2026 at the gallery on South Halsted Street in Chicago. Entry is free with membership; WMG has presented hundreds of exhibitions since 1992 and remains one of the longest-running feminist art spaces in the United States. — Deadline: October 3, 2026. Fee: Free for members. Prize: Group exhibition.

item.title: 51st Juried Annual Exhibition · Miller Art Museum
item.description: The Miller Art Museum in Sturgeon Bay opens its 51st Juried Annual, the Door County institution’s long-running survey of two-dimensional work by artists living in Wisconsin. It is open to artists 18 and over at every career stage, from emerging to established professional, and accepts original hangable 2D work in any media made within the past two years — photography very much included; the 2026 prospectus cover pairs Nika McKagen’s silver gelatin print with an oil painting. A panel of jurors reviews projected digital entries, and $1,950 in cash awards is presented at the opening reception on September 18: the Gerhard Miller Award of Excellence ($500), three Special Merit Awards ($250 each), three Juror’s Choice Awards ($200 each) and the Bonnie Hartmann Award for Outstanding Creativity ($100). Work may not exceed 48 x 48 x 5 inches including framing, must be a single unit (no diptychs or triptychs) and cannot have been shown previously in Door County; giclée and other reproductions are not eligible, nor is work made under a teacher’s direction in a class or workshop. The exhibition runs September 18 to November 7, 2026. Work may or may not be offered for sale; the museum retains a 40% commission on sales. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: $1,950 in awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Día de Muertos 2026 — Remembering Is Resistance · Firehouse Art Center
item.description: For its 2026 Día de Muertos exhibition, Recordar es Resistir / Remembering Is Resistance, Longmont’s Firehouse Art Center pairs artists with community members affected by US immigration policy so that each work carries a real story, told safely and anonymously. Selected artists meet their partner between August 24 and October 1 and translate that person’s words and experience into a piece for the Main Gallery, where the show sits as both reflection and provocation. Accepted mediums include photography, digital art, painting, drawing, collage, mixed media, text-based work, sculpture, installation, fibre and touchable or interactive work. The centre asks for practices that confront, reflect on or challenge political realities, global or deeply personal, and states plainly that credentials matter less than passion and messaging. Applicants send a single PDF holding a 200-word bio, a 200-word statement and five images. There is no entry fee. The call is addressed to artists in the Longmont area aged 18 and over, and work is hand-delivered on October 5 and 6. Community members need no paperwork and are compensated for their time; translators are provided for anyone who prefers to apply or work in another language. The Firehouse waives its commission entirely and splits any sale equally between artist and community member. The exhibition runs October 9 to November 1, 2026, opening with a reception on October 9. — Deadline: August 10, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: She Speaks · Tolleson Art Gallery
item.description: Juried exhibition at the Tolleson Art Gallery — a free exhibition space inside Tolleson Public Library, west of Phoenix — celebrating the creativity and artistic voices of Arizona women. Artists who are women or who identify as female are invited to share work reflecting their experiences, ideas and creative vision across all styles and themes; photography is explicitly welcome alongside painting, sculpture, mixed media, digital and textile work. Entry is free and open to Arizona artists of all backgrounds and experience levels. Each selected artist receives a $100 stipend to exhibit, rising to $575 for artists who also present a public program of at least an hour — a workshop, artist talk or demo (optional, not required to submit). The gallery also runs a visitor drawing during the exhibition in which one attendee receives an exhibited artwork purchased for up to $500. Submissions include a brief artist statement of up to 250 words connecting the work to the theme. On view October 23 – December 10, 2026. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $575 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Open Call: Main Gallery 2027/2028
item.description: The Firehouse Art Center in Longmont, Colorado is accepting proposals for its 2027/28 exhibition calendar. Housed in a National Historic Landmark building with two exhibition spaces and over 1,000 square feet, the free-admission contemporary art centre draws more than 10,000 visitors a year and has been voted Best Art Gallery in East Boulder County ten years running. Solo exhibition proposals from established and emerging artists in all mediums are welcome, as are group exhibitions and curatorial proposals. An exhibitions committee of artists, arts administrators, business professionals, curators and collectors reviews submissions; preference goes to culturally relevant work with a unique perspective that offers a diverse art experience, and cutting-edge contemporary and multi-disciplinary practices are strongly encouraged. Open to all artists in the continental US, with a stated commitment to artists across race, gender, gender variance, sexual orientation, national origin, age, religion, political affiliation and disability. Teams submit one résumé of no more than one page per member. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2027 Call for Exhibit Proposals · Museum of Northern California Art
item.description: The Museum of Northern California Art (monca) in Chico invites Northern California artists to propose a solo or small group exhibition for its Phillips Gallery, a 32 by 27 foot space. Four slots are offered across 2027, running six to eight weeks each between March 2027 and January 2028, with opening receptions on the Friday of the first week. Artwork must have been produced primarily in Northern California and the artist must currently live in one of the eligible counties; work previously exhibited at monca is not eligible and AI-generated work is excluded. Applications are reviewed by monca's exhibition committee of six artists and collectors, and ask for 8 to 12 images of proposed or representative works, an artist statement, a proposal narrative setting out the vision and thematic focus of the show (including any equipment or electrical needs), and a CV. Artists install and deinstall their own work. The museum does not actively market artwork but keeps a price list at reception and takes 50% commission on any sales. — Deadline: September 12, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Echoes of Valor · Artspiration Frederick
item.description: Artspiration Frederick's first veteran art exhibition, on view in the Artspiration Gallery in Frederick, Maryland from November 6 to 29, 2026, honouring the creative voices and lived experiences of military veterans, military families, and artists exploring themes of military service. Original work in any visual medium is welcome, including photography, printmaking, painting, sculpture, fibre art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art, and the exhibition seeks a diverse range of voices, perspectives and techniques. Eligible artists must be a US military veteran of any branch, active duty, reserve or National Guard, a military family member, or a civilian artist whose work addresses military or veteran themes; entrants must reside in the continental US. Up to three pieces may be submitted and all three may be selected. Two-dimensional work must be framed and wired for hanging (no sawtooth hangers). Accepted work is dropped off October 26–27 or shipped to arrive by October 26, with an artists' reception on November 14. Accepted images are also shown in a concurrent online exhibit. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 35 Under 35 — 2nd Annual Juried Exhibition · Blacksburg Regional Art Association
item.description: Second annual 35 Under 35 exhibition from the Blacksburg Regional Art Association, a 150-member group founded in 1950, in collaboration with community galleries and the Center for the Arts at Virginia Tech. The show exists to put emerging artists on the walls of established gallery and museum spaces and to help them find their way into the wider art community of curators, gallery owners and collectors. Thirty-five works are selected and shown November 2 to 20, 2026 at the Center for the Arts on the Virginia Tech campus, with an artist and awards reception on November 20. Juror Laura K. Higgins, Curator of the Permanent Collection and Special Projects Officer at the Taubman Museum of Art — previously at Tanya Bonakdar Gallery, Gladstone Gallery and Petzel in New York — presents Best in Show ($300), 2nd Place ($200), 3rd Place ($100) and honourable mentions at her discretion. Open to artists living in Virginia who have not turned 35 by November 2, 2026; any medium except AI-generated work. The $5 fee covers up to three works. Two-dimensional work must not exceed 40 inches in either direction. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: The Unexpected Portrait · Workshop13
item.description: Juried exhibition at ArtWorks Gallery, run by Workshop13, a nonprofit cultural arts and learning centre in Ware, Massachusetts. Artists are asked to deviate from formal posing and realistic representation, focusing instead on emotion, identity, memory, action or unconventional subject matter through modern techniques, stylised depiction or abstract interpretation of the sitter. Open to most physical media, photography included — electronic media cannot be accommodated, and AI-generated work, work created under instruction and work previously juried into an ArtWorks Gallery show are ineligible. Up to three original pieces per artist; the gallery may cap acceptances at two per artist depending on space. Juried by printmaker and teaching artist Julie Lapping Rivera. Accepted 2-D work must be framed and wired, hand-delivered or shipped with a prepaid return label. Exhibition runs 19 September – 17 October 2026, with an opening reception on 19 September. The gallery takes 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: $25 (1 work) / $35 (up to 3). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: West Coast Biennial 2027 · Turtle Bay Exploration Park
item.description: Ninth edition of Turtle Bay Exploration Park's juried West Coast Biennial, held in the museum galleries in Redding, California. Juror Karlo Henry Velazquez Fernandez — artist, curator, founder of The Art Hunger and Arts Director for Viva Downtown Redding — will select between 30 and 50 works for the exhibition. Painting, printmaking, drawing, photography, sculpture and mixed media are all accepted. Open to artists living in California, Oregon, Washington and Alaska, who may enter up to three works made within three years of the deadline. Cash awards are presented at the opening: Best of Show $3,000, First Prize $1,750, Second $900, Third $650, plus Honorable Mention and People's Choice awards of $325 each. The exhibition runs 29 January – 18 April 2027, opening with an artists' reception and juror talk. — Deadline: November 6, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: $3,000 + exhibition.

item.title: Artist Grant — November 2026 Cycle
item.description: An unrestricted $1,200 USD grant awarded to one visual artist three times a year, running since 2017. There is no proposal to write: applicants email a link to their website or three to five images of recent work along with a CV, resume or short bio. Open to visual artists aged 18 and over anywhere in the world working in painting, drawing, sculpture, ceramics, printmaking, photography, mixed media, installation and new or alternative visual art forms; film, video, music, theatre and dance are excluded, and past winners may not reapply. Grantees are featured on the Artist Grant website and social channels. Results are sent within six to eight weeks of the deadline. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: $1,200.

item.title: Reverie Magazine — Issue VI
item.description: Open submissions for the sixth issue of Reverie, an international independent literary and arts magazine whose stated mission is to promote education and amplify the voices of marginalised communities through literature and fine arts. Alongside poetry, prose and short fiction, the magazine reads visual art in all forms — contemporary photography, digital illustration, scans of painting and documentation of physical craft. Artists may send up to five high-resolution pieces as PNG, PDF or JPG to the editors by email, with a 50-word bio in the body of the message. Submissions are free and open worldwide. Previously published work is accepted if the prior publication is credited, and simultaneous submissions are welcome. Reverie asks for first publishing and archival rights; all rights revert to the maker on publication. Editors respond in about a month. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Cite the Past, Sight the Stars — Wigwell Lodge Residency · The Photographers' Gallery
item.description: Two-month fully funded residency at Wigwell Lodge in Derbyshire, run by The Photographers' Gallery in partnership with The Ampersand Foundation, for artists working with expanded photography and digital practices. Framed by photography's 200th anniversary, the call takes a set of speculative starting points — the Mnemosyne Atlas, the Voyager Golden Record, StarDisk, Inverted World Labs — and invites proposals that test ideas rather than deliver finished work. Suggested threads include image-making and celestial fictions, institutional archives, photography's relationship to computational culture, deep time, cosmic and earthly debris, transmissions and satellite imagery, and digital twins and AI world models. The residency provides accommodation and studio space at Wigwell Lodge, a £1,000 monthly stipend, a £1,000 production budget, up to £500 towards travel, promotion, and curatorial and administrative support, with the potential to develop into a commission for 2027/2028 and a public presentation at the Gallery or a partner venue. Open to individual artists over 18 with the legal right to work in the UK; no visa sponsorship is available. The residency runs 2 February – 31 March 2027. — Deadline: September 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £2,000 stipend + £1,000 production budget.

item.title: Brooklyn Darkroom Artist in Residence 2027
item.description: Travelling residency for analog photographers run by Brooklyn Darkroom, a New York State 501(c)(3) that supports film-based practitioners with photography and travel resources. Selected artists get up to one month on the road in 'Infared', a fully equipped 2023 Winnebago Solis 59P pop-top camper van, a $4,000 stipend covering travel, living and materials while travelling, and access to the organisation's analog darkroom in Brooklyn for development, printing and finishing, plus optional post-production support. Applications are open to all artists working in analog photography, and experimental collaborations are welcome; past residents include Curran Hatleberg, Irina Rozovsky, Mark Steinmetz, Jocelyn Lee and Dylan Hausthor. Applying costs $15 through SlideRoom. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: $15. Prize: $4,000 stipend + One-month camper van residency.

item.title: Liberty Art Award 2026 · Liberty Specialty Markets
item.description: Two-year professional development, exhibition and sales programme for recent UK art graduates, run by fine art insurer Liberty Specialty Markets with Parker Harris. Launched in 2018 and previously limited to four institutions, the award opens to graduates nationwide for the first time this year. Each selected artist receives a £1,000 participation fee, a contribution to travel expenses, collection and return of work, insurance in transit and on display, and the chance to exhibit and sell work at Liberty's office in the Walkie Talkie building in Fenchurch Street, London, from September 2026 to August 2028. The development programme includes at least four one-to-one mentoring sessions with Penny Harris of Parker Harris, group visits to Frieze, London Art Fair, Collect and London Print Fair, seminars from gallerists, funders, curators, critics and legal advisors, and task-based work on proposal writing and funding applications. The programme closes with an awards ceremony in spring 2028. Any medium is eligible, including photography, moving image, print, sculpture, paint and textile; work must be available for the full two years and shown in a corporate setting. Open to students who graduated in 2025 and 2026 from across the UK. — Deadline: July 29, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £7,500 in prizes + £1,000 participation fee.

item.title: The People's Garden · Open Eye Gallery
item.description: Rolling open call from Open Eye Gallery in Liverpool, gathering the public's own garden pictures for The People's Garden, a growing display within the gallery's exhibition Is This A Garden? (26 June – 31 August 2026). The gallery welcomes family album photographs as readily as recent pictures — a family gathering, a football game, a visiting puppy, your own garden or a public one. Selected images are printed and added to the exhibition as they arrive, so earlier submissions hang for longer. Send up to three digital images at the highest resolution possible, 30MB maximum each, by email with your name, postcode, an optional text of up to 100 words about the images, and a statement confirming the images are your own and you have the right to show them publicly. No AI-generated or digitally manipulated images. Open to anyone over 18 currently based in the UK; one submission per person. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: In The Practice of Seeing — High School Section · Jacksonville State University
item.description: Free national juried photography exhibition for high school students, running as the teen section of Jacksonville State University's In the Practice of Seeing and shown in the Roundhouse Gallery at Hammond Hall alongside the main exhibition, 27 August – 24 September 2026. The brief treats photography as an active process of perception rather than a neutral record — seeing shaped by attention, context, memory and cultural framework. Open to all photographic processes including digital, film, alternative processes, mixed media incorporating photography, and photographic installations; every entry must originate from a camera-based capture or a cameraless photographic method such as photograms, cyanotypes or wet plate. Open to students aged 13–17. Up to 3 images, free to enter; framed work no larger than 16 × 20 inches, with artists responsible for shipping or delivery. Winners receive an Adorama Photo sponsored gift card. — Deadline: August 6, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Adorama gift card + Exhibition.

item.title: Eyes & Hands: Celebrating Frederick's Deaf heART · Artspiration Frederick
item.description: Juried exhibition for Deaf, Hard of Hearing and CODA (Children of Deaf Adults) artists at Artspiration Frederick, a nonprofit community art centre in Frederick, Maryland, marking Deaf Awareness Month. Artists are invited to submit original work in any visual medium including photography, painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, fiber art, ceramics, mixed media and digital art, with the show seeking a deliberately wide range of voices, perspectives, techniques and subject matter. On view in the Artspiration Frederick Gallery 5–27 September 2026. Open to visual artists 16 and older who are Deaf, Hard of Hearing and/or CODA and reside in the continental US; 1–3 images at 300 dpi for jury review. Two-dimensional work must be framed and wired for hanging — no sawtooth hangers. — Deadline: August 15, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Americana · Crooked Tree Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition in the East and West Carnegie Galleries at Crooked Tree Arts Center in Traverse City, Michigan, asking what America looks like through your eyes. Beyond the familiar shorthand of rolling farmland, front porches, Main Streets, county fairs and open roads, the call invites work that celebrates, questions, reinterprets or expands American identity — drawing on place, community, music, labour, history, culture, memory, migration, celebration, resilience and everyday life. Works may be literal or abstract, traditional or experimental; all media are welcome, photography included, and artists at every career stage are encouraged. Open to artists 18+ resident in the US Great Lakes region — if your state has a Great Lakes shoreline, you are eligible. Up to three works made in the last three years, $30 entry. Exhibition 4 September – 3 October 2026. — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Leela Mukherjee Artist-Educator Grant 2026 · Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation
item.description: Third edition of the Mrinalini Mukherjee Foundation's annual grant for artist-educators in India, instituted in 2024 with the support of the Welham Old Boys' Society and named for the modernist sculptor and teacher Leela Mukherjee, who introduced art to generations of students at Welham Boys' School in Dehradun. Three grants of Rs. 1 lakh each support practitioners running an art education project with school-aged children (5–18), inside or outside the classroom, over a period of up to 12 months. The foundation looks for projects that fold local knowledge, lived environments and everyday experience into teaching methods, and for artists whose own practice and pedagogy inform one another. Proposals should describe the student group and why the artist works with them, the innovative strategies and artistic methods proposed, expected outcomes after 12 months, a tentative budget and a timeline. Applicants must be Indian citizens resident in India and over 18; collectives may apply if every member qualifies. The foundation's grants are restricted to the visual arts, which include lens-based practice. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,200 (Rs. 1 lakh) × 3 grants.

item.title: III Artist Fund Grant 2026
item.description: Artist-run fund set up by Jamie Zimchek and Shannon Cleere, who met in graduate school and created the grant to support artists navigating a post-graduate practice at a moment when work that challenges dominant narratives faces scrutiny, funding difficulties, and censorship. A $1,000 unrestricted grant goes to one artist who holds an MFA in Visual Art awarded May 2025 or later and can demonstrate a strong research-based practice responding to contemporary contexts. Multidisciplinary and conceptual artists working in photography, drawing, painting, sculpture, printmaking, textile, installation, performance, sound, video and new media are all encouraged to apply. The recipient is asked only to give a short artist talk within six months, recorded and posted to the fund's website. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $1,000.
